what: Measurement of struct vinfo at the moment PE_init_platform() has returned in arm_init, in QEMU, and the controls for the 'lumia-early-bar' instrument that was built on the assumption that vinfo is usable there

method.kernel: the build from run 45927960099, which carries the lumia-early-bar instrument
method.breakpoint: _wfe_timeout_configure (0xfffffff00740a2c0), the first statement after PE_init_platform(FALSE, args)
method.read: struct vinfo at 0xfffffff007af17e8, 128 bytes, via the fixture's --read-at

controls.positive: boot with 'lumia-early-bar': 0 pixels of the bar colour in rows 120-135; the kernel still reached root-wait
controls.negative: boot without it: 0 pixels in those rows (as expected), kernel reached root-wait
controls.safety: with the argument present the kernel did not fault at the instrument: the guard (v_baseaddr != 0) skipped the store and the boot continued to the same place as without it

source: pexpert/arm/pe_init.c: the console is created by PE_create_console(), which calls PE_initialize_console() only when PE_state.video.v_display is set

osfmk/console/video_console.c initialize_screen(): with kernel_map == VM_MAP_NULL it calls ml_io_map_unmappable() and sets new_vinfo.v_baseaddr from the result; before arm_vm_init that map does not exist
osfmk/arm/arm_init.c: PE_create_console() is called at line 571, i.e. after arm_vm_init() at line 516 -- the framebuffer becomes writable only there
conclusion: vinfo is entirely zero when PE_init_platform() returns: there is no address to draw through at that point, and never was.
The console, and with it the framebuffer mapping, is created later in arm_init, after the VM work. So no framebuffer output is possible before arm_vm_init by construction rather than by accident.

The early bar is therefore not a valid instrument for the handset: a missing bar would say nothing about whether the kernel reached that point. It stays in the tree behind its boot argument because it is harmless and documents the attempt.
An observable before arm_vm_init needs either a mapping made from the kernel's own bootstrap page tables (start.s) or a non-video channel such as a RAM mailbox that survives a warm reset.
